messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient: 51 year old female

Admission: Shimane University Hospital
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Medical History: Insomnia, auditory hallucinations, delusions of persecution

Hospital Course: The patient was admitted to Shimane University Hospital with auditory hallucinations and delusions of persecution at the age of 49. Examination showed an autistic state, catatonic stupor, and deterioration of social functioning. The Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale (PANSS) was used to evaluate her psychiatric symptoms. Other routine laboratory examinations were within normal limits. Risperidone was started and her symptoms gradually decreased. However, at the age of 51, the patient developed psychomotor excitement and auditory hallucinations which led to a catatonic stupor. Haloperidol and perospirone were prescribed but worsened her symptoms. Modified electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) was started as a supplementary strategy and her symptoms gradually improved. The patient became almost symptom-free after the seventh ECT so the treatment was discontinued. During ECT, her prescription was not changed. 

Outcome: The patient's symptoms improved and she was transferred to another hospital for further training in social skills.

Follow-up Recommendations: The patient should continue her follow-up care with her psychiatrist and attend regular therapy sessions to monitor her symptoms and adjust medications as needed.

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
Persistent auditory hallucinations and persecutory delusions with catatonic stupor, treated with antipsychotics and ECT, point to schizophrenia (catatonic features). This sits in chapter F, mental and behavioural disorders. The category is F20, schizophrenia.

CODE: F20
